title: SII Vol. 3 No. 89 — Tillasthanam
location_detail: On The South Wall Of The Central Shrine In The Ghritasthanesvara Temple At Tillasthanam

title: SII Vol. 3 No. 90 — Tirumeyjnanam
location_detail: On The North Wall Of The Central Shrine In The Jnanaparamesvara Temple At Tirumeyjnanam
summary: This inscription is dated in the 2nd year of Rajakesarivarman and records that the assembly of Nalur, a brahmadeya of Serrur-kurram, sold for 25 kasu, the angadikkuli, i.e., the market fees of the bazaar street, to the temple Tirumayanam

title: SII Vol. 3 No. 91 — Tirunagesvaram
location_detail: On A Pillar Lying In The Mandapa In A Street At Tirunagesvaram
date_text: This is a record, in archaic characters, of Rajakesarivarman (perhaps Aditya I.) dated in his 2nd year
summary: It registers gifts made by the merchants (nagarattar) of Kumaramaratandapuram to meet the cost of repairs of the enclosure (called) Maunakumaramartandan and the gopura of Miladudaiyarpalli

title: SII Vol. 3 No. 199
location_detail: In the word Miladudaiyarpalli we may have a possible reference to the Saiva saint Meypporunayanar also called Miladudaiyar
summary: of the Madras Epigraphical collection for 1907 it appears that Kumaramartandan was a surname of the Pallava king Nandipporaiyar

title: SII Vol. 3 No. 92 — Vedal
location_detail: On A Boulder In Front Of A Natural Cave At Vedal
summary: This inscription is dated in the 14th year of Rajakesarivarman and provides for feeding the female Jain ascetic Kanakavirakurattiyar, who was a disciple of Gunakirtti-Bhatara, and her pupils
